strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear differentiation between RLVR and SFT optimization dynamics, grounded in recent mechanistic literature
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple model scales (1.5B-32B), domains (math, medical, coding), and benchmarks with both in-distribution and out-of-distribution evaluation
Solid mechanistic analysis including complementarity of geometric priors (Table 5), spectral structure verification (Figure 6), and alignment metrics (Table 6) that support core claims
Consistent empirical improvements across most benchmarks with good ablation studies (Table 4) and hyperparameter robustness analysis (Figures 4, 7)
Practical efficiency gains: 99.5% parameter reduction, 19.9% speed improvement, and 28.5% VRAM reduction compared to full fine-tuning
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: geometric masking, SVD initialization, and residual freezing are well-established techniques; contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Insufficient theoretical justification for geometric prior construction: spectral prior appears circular (using rank-r approx to define mask), Euclidean prior lacks RLVR-specific motivation, choice of union over intersection not justified, sparsity ratio ρ=0.2 appears arbitrary
Lack of statistical rigor: modest improvements (1-3% on many benchmarks), single random runs, no error bars or significance tests making it difficult to assess if differences are meaningful
Narrow experimental scope: only RLVR with verifiable rewards in reasoning domains; unclear generalization to dialogue, open-ended RL, or reward model-based approaches

Incomplete comparison with SparseFT: achieves competitive results (Tables 1-2), per-iteration speedup only 10.8% slower (Table 3), contradicting claim that sparse methods fail to translate sparsity into hardware speedups
Missing statistical validation across multiple runs and no ablation studies on key hyperparameter choices (e.g., why ρ=0.2 and r=16?)
Propositions B.1-B.2 are standard results lacking novel theoretical insight into why this approach suits RLVR-specific optimization geometry

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear identification of a genuine gap in RLVR optimization geometry vs. SFT-optimized PEFT methods
Principled technical design grounded in mechanistic insights: spectral priors suppress high-curvature directions while Euclidean priors target plastic regions
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple scales (1.5B-32B), architectures (Qwen, Llama), and domains (math, medical, coding) with consistent improvements
Convincing convergence speed analysis (Figure 3) showing faster training with higher plateaus; robust stability under aggressive learning rates (Figure 5)
Thorough mechanistic analysis: spectral analysis validates low-rank structure (Figure 6), geometric metrics confirm structure preservation (Table 6, NSS≈0.09 vs PiSSA≈0.39)
Clear ablations demonstrating necessity of geometry-aware initialization; complementary masking priors with low overlap (Jaccard≈0.13) validates dual-prior design
Significant practical efficiency: 99.5% parameter reduction, 19.9% training speedup, 28.5% VRAM savings with hardware efficiency (unlike sparse methods)
Strong out-of-distribution generalization across HumanEval, GPQA, MMLU suggesting learned representations remain robust
Clear presentation with intuitive figures (Figures 1-2 effectively compare approaches) and comprehensive appendices enabling reproducibility
Mathematically sound: Eckart-Young theorem justifies SVD initialization, Proposition 2 proves function preservation, gradient analysis correctly derives manifold constraints
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: SVD-based initialization, frozen residuals, and spectral/magnitude masking are individually established; contribution is primarily their combination for RLVR rather than novel methods
Moderate empirical improvements: typical 5-15% relative gains over LoRA/MiLoRA (e.g., AIME24: 23.75 vs 19.58/20.42); some benchmarks show smaller margins making absolute gains incremental
Experimental rigor concerns: all results appear to be single random runs without error bars or confidence intervals, making statistical significance of reported differences difficult to assess

Masking strategy lacks principled justification: why union of priors is optimal unclear; choice of quantile thresholds (ρ) appears empirical without thorough exploration of alternatives (intersection, weighting)

Scope constraints: experiments focus exclusively on RLVR with verifiable rewards in reasoning tasks; generalizability to other RL settings (preference learning, continuous control) explicitly acknowledged as unvalidated
Incomplete hyperparameter analysis: fixed ρ=0.2 and r=16 as defaults; sensitivity analysis relegated to appendix; interaction effects between hyperparameters and model scale not explored
Limited baseline diversity: missing comparisons with recent adaptive PEFT methods; DoRA, AdaLoRA, and other recent variants not included alongside LoRA/PiSSA/MiLoRA

Missing ablations: no layer-wise analysis identifying which parameter types benefit most; no investigation of when geometry-aware initialization provides largest advantage; limited discussion of failure cases
Reproducibility constraints: uses proprietary Qwen3 models and internal DeepMath-103K dataset limiting external validation; code release plans not mentioned

Theoretical gaps: why SVD of WGeo captures optimal update directions lacks formal justification; heavy-tailed spectrum property shown empirically (Figure 6b) but not proven; mechanism for preventing 'erosion' of pre-trained structure only validated by NSS metric
